title: solution.tex Convention 2.4: crosscut-lengthening is an imported hypothesis, not condition (iii) — faithfulness of S1

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Location:** solution.tex, \S1, Convention `conv:squeeze` (and the Remark/justification immediately following), with downstream dependence in Lemma `lem:expand` and Lemma `lem:bound`.

**The issue (faithfulness / load-bearing assumption).** Convention `conv:squeeze` reads the hypotheses on a realizing map $f$ as a *squeeze map*: on each clean triangle $\tau$, $f|_\tau$ **strictly shortens the distinguished (boundary) edge AND strictly lengthens the two crosscutting edges**. The write-up then states explicitly:

> "We flag explicitly that property (b) [the crosscutting edges are lengthened] is part of the hypothesis on $F$, not a consequence of (a) [condition (iii)] alone; indeed (a) by itself does not pin down a threshold (one may shrink everything and embed a tiny band)."

So the solution itself acknowledges that the crosscut-lengthening is an **added hypothesis**, not derivable from condition (iii). This is exactly the kind of definitional drift that is most dangerous: the validity of Statement 1 depends entirely on whether the *official* definition of a "realized" $\beta$ (i.e. the official reading of conditions (i)/(ii)/(iii), "clean triangulation", and "squeeze map") includes the lengthening of crosscutting edges.

**Why this is decisive.** Both load-bearing length lemmas of S1 use the lengthening:
- Lemma `lem:expand` ("squeeze maps expand crosscuts") uses $\|V\|<\|V'\|$ and $\|W\|<\|W'\|$ (the crosscutting edges $[p,a],[p,b]$ are lengthened) together with $\|V-W\|>\|V'-W'\|$. All three inequalities of \eqref{eq:squeeze} are genuinely used to derive $V\!\cdot\!W<V'\!\cdot\!W'$ and hence crosscut expansion.
- Lemma `lem:bound` uses $\ell(f(A))>\ell(A)$ and $\ell(f(B))>\ell(B)\ge1$, i.e. crosscut expansion again.

If the official notion of "realized" imposes only condition (iii) = "every non-degenerate boundary subarc is strictly shortened" (the distinguished-edge part), then S1 as written proves a lower bound only for the **strictly smaller** class of squeeze maps, and the claimed threshold $\sqrt3$ for the *stated* class is NOT established. As the solution itself notes, without the crosscut hypothesis there is no positive threshold at all (shrink to embed any small band).

**Aggravating factor.** problem.tex (the provided statement) does **not** contain the definitions of conditions (i),(ii),(iii), "realized", "clean triangulation", or "squeeze map" — these strings appear only inside the proof, never in a definition block (verified by search). Hence the authoritative meaning of the hypotheses is not available in-repo, and the solution has had to *reconstruct/assume* it. The reconstruction must be checked against the source.

**What is needed to close.**
1. Obtain the exact official definition of "realized" / conditions (i)-(iii) / "squeeze map" / "clean triangulation". State it verbatim.
2. If the lengthening of crosscutting edges IS part of the official definition: cite it precisely at Convention `conv:squeeze`, and the issue dissolves (Convention 2.4 becomes a quotation, not an assumption).
3. If it is NOT: either (a) prove crosscut-lengthening as a consequence of (i)+(ii)+(iii) (appears impossible), or (b) explicitly restate the theorem as a statement about the squeeze class. The current write-up must not silently strengthen the hypothesis.
